Subject: URGENT: webhook failures to Redwood prod - impacted customers

Hi Jordan/Camila,

Since 08:50 PDT we're seeing ~20% of outbound webhooks from Nimbus failing with 502/504 against Redwood's webhook ingestion endpoints (https://api.redwood.ai/webhook/v1/...). This is impacting two customers in our trial cohort (Acme Media, Volt Analytics) — events are delayed by ~30-120s and many are being retried multiple times.

Attached a short delivery trace and a screenshot of the 502. Can you confirm whether there's a service degradation on your side or if something in our payload shape is triggering a proxy error? We're on an active onboarding call with Acme at 09:30; this needs priority.

Thanks,
Evan

Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: webhook failures to Redwood prod - impacted customers

Jordan/Evan — thanks for the ping. Quick notes from initial triage: 

- Observed spike in 502/504 from the edge proxy cluster between 08:48–09:10 PDT. Error signatures match partial upstream timeouts rather than payload validation rejects.
- Correlating with autoscaler activity for several Dedicated pools: a burst of scale-out created a small routing window where some requests were routed to a warmup path that didn't have the full HTTP keepalive config. That path times out on larger-ish payloads (~>12KB).
- Impact surface: Nimbus's typical webhook payloads are near that size for event batches; two onboarding customers' ingestion rates amplify the symptom.

Immediate mitigation we can apply now (recommended):
1) Enable temporary "prefer-primary" routing for Nimbus customer tag to avoid warmup path (low-risk rollback).
2) Increase ingress proxy timeout for 300s for that tag and apply stricter retry/backoff at the client side (we can push a config patch that takes ~7–10m).
3) Flag for infra to adjust autoscaler warmup to pre-initialize keepalives (medium-term fix).

I'll prepare a short runbook excerpt and push a config patch. Vivek, can you take run-of-change and execute steps 1/2? Evan — if you can send a short failing payload sample (no PII) that helps us validate before/after.

Camila

----
Attachments: runbook-excerpt.txt

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Shaw <evan.shaw@nimbuslabs.com>, Priya Menon <priya@nimbuslabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:41:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: webhook failures to Redwood prod - impacted customers

On it — executing mitigation now. Summary of actions taken at 09:39 PDT:
- Applied "prefer-primary" routing for partner tag nimbus-prod (instant).
- Increased ingress proxy timeout to 300s for that tag and deployed a config patch to the edge cluster (completed by 09:40).
- Restarted the small pool of warmup workers to pick up keepalive settings (rolling restart, ~2 mins).
- Opened Jira SUP-4821 to track follow-up engineering work (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-4821).

Evan/Priya: please validate whether you still see 502/504 on your side; if you can, provide a representative failed payload (sanitized). We'll keep the temporary settings for 6 hours and revert when the autoscaler warmup fix is merged.

Vivek

Two asks from Nimbus leadership:
1) We need a short incident summary + postmortem and confirmation of whether this counts as a breach of the integration SLA (their contract references 99.9% delivery availability for onboarding traffic).
2) If SLA is breached, can we agree a standard credit process? We can provide customer impact logs and timestamps.

Happy to join a quick 15-min postmortem with your infra/ops lead.

Evan
